requirement_text: Holders of a Swiss maturité gymnasiale 'are accepted at EPFL with no other condition nor capacity limitation in the first year' of their chosen program. They may voluntarily take the preparatory Cours de mathématiques spéciales (CMS) while retaining their right to direct first-year acceptance if they choose not to continue with CMS.
source_authority_note: epfl.ch is EPFL's official domain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: Included for contrast with the international pathways below, even though this specific record applies to domestic Swiss maturité holders.

requirement_text: EU/EFTA secondary certificate holders must show: mathematics and physics studied 'at the highest possible level'; at least six of seven required subjects present on transcripts (mathematics, physics, native language, second language, chemistry/biology, history/geography/economics, and applied math/CS/philosophy); final grades in math and physics 'at least 80% of the maximum grade'; and an overall average 'at least 80% of the maximum grade.' Acceptance is 'within the places available' based on general-average ranking (i.e. competitive, not a guaranteed seat even if the threshold is met) — EPFL capped first-year intake at 3,000 students from Fall 2025 for at least four years.
limitations: The 80% thresholds and 'within places available' ranking language came through an AI-summarized WebFetch extraction rather than a raw-HTML read; treated as extracted_summary rather than verbatim. Recommend re-verifying exact percentage figures directly on the EPFL page before using in any student-facing numeric claim.
researcher_notes: Note the important nuance: meeting the 80% threshold does not guarantee admission — it only qualifies the applicant to compete for a place within the capacity cap. This is a ranked/competitive admission, not a pure pass/fail threshold, despite superficially reading like one.

requirement_text: British qualification holders must study mathematics, physics, and chemistry/biology/computer science 'at Advanced Levels and/or Advanced Highers' with grades 'at least A and/or 1'. GCSE/Standard Grade level must include English, a second language, and history/geography. The French B2 requirement (see separate language record) also applies.
limitations: Extracted via AI-summarized WebFetch; recommend re-verifying exact grade thresholds directly before using in a student-facing numeric claim.

requirement_text: International Baccalaureate holders must achieve a total of 'at least 38 out of 42 (excluding bonus points)', with mathematics and physics grades 'at least 6 out of 7'. Higher Level (HL) subjects required: mathematics, physics, and chemistry/biology/computer science. At Standard or Higher Level: two modern languages and one of history/geography/economics/philosophy. Acceptance is 'within the places available' (competitive ranking, not a guaranteed seat).
limitations: 38/42 and 6/7 figures came through an AI-summarized WebFetch extraction, not a raw-HTML read; flagged for re-verification before use in a precise student-facing numeric claim. This is notably higher than the IB threshold UNIGE states for its own bachelor admission (32/42 minimum, per UNIGE file) — this is NOT a conflict, since these are two different institutions independently setting their own thresholds on top of the same base IB-recognition framework, not two sources describing the same institution's rule differently.

requirement_text: EPFL considers that level B2 in French (CEFR) is required to follow its Bachelor's programmes; level C1 is highly recommended.

Applicants from non-EU/EFTA/UK countries whose certificate doesn't meet direct-admission criteria must either (a) enter the CMS (Cours de Mathématiques Spéciales) preparatory year — not direct first-year entry — 'within the places available', meeting similar academic standards to EU/EFTA applicants (approx. 80% in math/physics and overall average), with 'passing the CMS is equivalent to passing the entrance examination'; or (b) register directly for EPFL's own entrance examination, which has 'no condition nor capacity limitation' on registration itself. The examination has scientific-subjects and general-knowledge-subjects components, and EPFL determines whether a candidate sits the 'full or reduced' version based on review of their school curriculum. EPFL 'strongly discourages applicants from taking the examination with the baccalaureate or any other secondary education as sole preparation.'
researcher_notes: Genuine entrance-exam pathway, not a numeric-score-threshold requirement — recorded as requirement_category_db='entrance_exam' rather than forcing a fake threshold. Note EPFL's entrance exam is functionally parallel to, but administratively distinct from, ETH Zurich's own entrance exam — see Switzerland-system file record REQ-2026-08-21-0011.

requirement_text: 'Applicants who do not hold one of the upper secondary school-leaving certificates or higher education diplomas listed above cannot be accepted' to EPFL's bachelor programs. Bachelor's degree holders from Swiss HES/FHS institutions or other Swiss universities are accepted 'with no condition nor capacity limitation' except in closely related fields; those with one completed university year elsewhere may apply for second-year admission 'following the evaluation of their application.'
researcher_notes: Recorded this exclusion clause explicitly rather than omitting it — an applicant whose certificate type isn't on EPFL's recognized list is not admissible at all, regardless of grades.

requirement_text: From Fall 2025, EPFL limits total first-year Bachelor intake to 3,000 students for at least four years. Guaranteed-admission categories (exempt from the capacity limitation) are: students repeating first year, Swiss maturité gymnasiale holders, and applicants who complete the CMS or pass the entrance examination.
limitations: The '4 years' duration of the cap was not independently cross-verified against a second page; treat the end-date of this policy as approximate.

requirement_text: EPFL does not offer a Bachelor's degree in Human Medicine. EPFL and UNIL jointly run a one-year gateway program allowing students who complete a Bachelor's in Biology or Life Sciences Engineering (bioengineering) at EPFL to apply into the Master's in Medicine program at UNIL; this is a Master's-level bridging pathway, not a Bachelor's-level medicine admission route, and it is not the EMS/numerus-clausus pathway used at ETH Zurich or UZH.
source_authority_note: actu.epfl.ch is EPFL's official news subdomain; not .edu/.ac./.gov.
limitations: Sourced from an EPFL news article rather than a formal admissions-regulations page; recommend re-verifying against EPFL/UNIL's formal inter-institutional agreement text if this pathway becomes decision-relevant for a specific student.
researcher_notes: Explicit honest negative finding requested by the task brief: EPFL has no Bachelor medicine program, so the EMS/entrance-exam medicine research does not apply to EPFL directly. Recorded rather than silently omitted.

requirement_text: Admission to the first year of a Bachelor's degree at EPFL 'depends on the upper-secondary leaving certificate you hold and its country of origin. Some diplomas can give direct access, while others may require additional steps such as an entrance examination.'
researcher_notes: General framing statement, included for completeness alongside the specific pathway records above.

deadline_text_verbatim: Applications can be submitted from mid-November to the 30th of April to start your studies at EPFL the following September.
cycle_label: Standard Bachelor application window (opens mid-November, closes April 30)
limitations: Recorded as a recurring annual pattern (mid-November opening, April 30 close) rather than tied to one specific year, since the source described it in general/recurring terms rather than naming one specific application year. cycle_year left null accordingly.

deadline_text_verbatim: for admission to the first year of the Bachelor's program, it is possible to apply between May 1st and July 31st provided that one holds an appropriate school certificate and that one fulfills at least one of the required conditions
cycle_label: Late-application window, first-year only, conditional eligibility
limitations: Eligibility for this late window is conditional (e.g. having applied elsewhere in Switzerland by April 30, late relocation to a Western Swiss canton, loss of employment after April 30, etc.) — see requirement records for the full condition list; not a general-purpose late-application option. Carries an additional CHF 150 preliminary tax. Upper-year (non-first-year) applicants are explicitly NOT eligible for this window.

deadline_text_verbatim: Scientific subjects: January 19–23, 2026 / General-knowledge subjects: August–September 2026
limitations: The general-knowledge sitting (Aug–Sept 2026) may not have concluded as of the real research date (2026-08-21) depending on its exact date within that window, which the source did not specify to the day.
